# My practicum story

The truth is that I have been thinking a few times about the practicum story because there has not been anything extraordinary or out of the ordinary since in the groups where I have been: 4 ESO and the 2 high school students there is no conflict whatsoever, a clear racial or cognitive diversity or anything else to highlight or expand on to construct this story.

I do want to remember that the first day I was, not nervous, but *very expectant* and the first few days I was extremely cautious with everything I did and said. The truth is that, in this observation phase, unless Carlos invited me to contribute more information to what he was explaining, I have limited myself to being in the back of the class observing and taking notes. My interventions have been to add comments or extra explanations that Carlos was giving in class, but I remember that on the third day of the first week I was already participating in Carlos's explanations. These interventions have grown over time as I gained more confidence in myself and the trust between Carlos and me.

In any case, I would like to expand on a couple of aspects that have caught my attention and have been a constant in the 3 groups and especially in the elective subjects. The first circumstance that caught my attention was that the **students are grouped in class by sex**, either to work in groups during the optional classes or simply to sit and follow the explanations of the non-optional classes. There was not a day that this situation was not repeated. This is facilitated by the fact that *Carlos does not create the groups*, but rather the students themselves group themselves together and this means that the groups always end up being the same, each one with their friends and separated by sex. This aspect of sex, I don't know if this is related to the fact that the school is religious or not since I have no criteria to compare with secular public schools.

In my opinion, this situation *impoverishes the exchange of different ideas*, and does not help a good and strong cohesion of all the components of the classroom and that ultimately *has an impact on the classroom environment and its management*. Reversing this dynamic could help create greater cohesion of the students as a group and obviously the group work would be greatly enriched by the diversity of ideas. Normally, friends have very similar ideas and working with friends is fine, but I think that in these stages it is impoverishing to always do group work with friends and separated by sex.

The other fact that caught my attention and I didn't like it at all is the **use of the laptop when it is not strictly necessary**. I have only described this circumstance in high school and I have been able to verify that many students are distracted doing other things such as playing, designing the Christmas card for the school contest while Carlos or another student is presenting their work on the stage.

I have discussed both aspects with Carlos, my tutor, and obviously he is aware of both circumstances. What surprises me most is that Carlos does not fight these situations to reverse them, given his vast experience with more than 35 years as a teacher always in the same school and that he is also an excellent teacher, with overwhelming control of the curriculum and unbeatable management of the teaching function. My internal conflict, or what I want to say in this story, is why with his experience he does nothing knowing that group work could be improved if the groups were designed by himself and on the other hand, not allowing the use of laptops when it is not strictly necessary.

::::: {style="display: flex; gap: 2em; align-items: stretch; justify-content: space-between;"}
::: {style="flex: 50%;"}
![Baccalaureate teachers' room](/images/practicum/sala-profes.png)
:::

::: {style="flex: 50%;"}
![Main entrance of the center](/images/practicum/entrada-sg.png)
:::
:::::

Possibly, at this point with his 35 years of experience, he is clear that there are battles that deserve to be fought (and I have seen some of him in class) and that other battles are not, like the circumstances that I have described. It is a topic that I did not want to talk about in depth with Carlos so as not to make him uncomfortable or cause him to think that it could call into question his teaching work, which I think is excellent, but I would have liked to have addressed this topic much more in depth with him to know why he does nothing to reverse these two situations.

What I did tell him when we were talking about the learning situations that I will have to prepare for the second phase of the practicum is that *I will design the work groups myself* to create heterogeneous groups by mixing students by sex and with the help of Carlos I will also include the academic performance parameter to cognitively balance the groups. I also told him that in my classes *I will ask students to keep their laptops off the table when it is not strictly necessary* to avoid confusion. In both cases, he told me that, without any problem, I will be able to manage my classes as I see fit. We will see what results heterogeneous groups give and if group cohesion and group work performance are actually improved. And I hope that the limitation of the use of laptops is not a cause of friction with the students trying to explain it to them in a coherent and beneficial way for them.

The icing on the cake at the end of the three weeks was that the 2nd year high school students said goodbye very warmly and asked me why I was leaving so early. I have to admit that I was surprised when they asked me why I was leaving so early, since I wasn't expecting it and the truth is that I really liked it.

# My inquiry journal in the practicum - Part 1

To begin or open my inquiry journal, it is necessary to begin by linking it with my account of the observation phase of the practicum to define the problem to be investigated. Within these quiet classrooms, as I have commented in my story, what has caught my attention the most during this observation phase has been that **immiscibility between sexes** and the **use of the laptop when it is not strictly necessary**. Of these two points, immiscibility between sexes would be my area of ​​interest that I want to work on and focus on during the intervention phase. It seems very important to me because, in my opinion, if this student behavior could be reversed, the improvement effects would have repercussions on the classroom environment, group cohesion, exchange of new and different ideas among them and ultimately greater academic performance and cognitive improvement by exposing students to new and different ideas beyond their friends. These results or potential improvement effects seem very important to me and for this reason I want to implement corrective measures to see if the academic performance of the students' group work can be improved, there is greater group cohesion regardless of gender and ultimately an academic improvement in general. Saying that the use of the laptop will be a minor issue than I think that talking and reaching an agreement with them so that they do not do it when it is not strictly necessary will be more than enough.

Therefore, having identified the problem that occurs both in 4th year of ESO and in the two high school groups through my three weeks of observation, now the most specific questions that I would like to investigate would be how and in what way to reverse the situation without being too disruptive. And on the other hand, the approach of my hypothesis is that grouping by sex for group work will be very beneficial for students in various aspects, from cognitive, human and academic performance.

I believe that the solution to this situation has a first clear option, which would be to create multilevel groups, creating heterogeneous groups based on the variable that I want to work on, which is the sex of the student, and a second working variable to balance these heterogeneous groups would be the individual cognitive performance of each student. In this second variable I will need Carlos's help (since he knows the students well) to cognitively balance the groups. In this way, the aim is to improve the teaching and learning process of students with the improvement of teaching practice through the implementation of multi-level heterogeneous groups.

# Other personal notes during the observation phase beyond the story

## My interventions as an observer

The truth is that in this observation phase, unless Carlos invited me to contribute more information to what he was explaining, I have limited myself to being in the back of the class observing and taking notes. My interventions have been to add comments or extra explanations that Carlos was giving in class, but I remember that on the third day of the first week I was already participating in Carlos's explanations. These interventions have grown over time as I gained more confidence in myself and the trust between Carlos and me. I have also helped supervise exams during those 4 days of quarterly and I have interacted a lot with the high school teachers since Carlos's activity in the ESO classes was limited to the subject of scientific culture of 4 of the ESO.

The truth is that this fact is the only 'non-optimal' point that I can put on the practices since it limits my interaction experience with the rest of the teaching staff to about 5 people with whom I have had direct contact within the high school teachers' room. The only interaction with the ESO teachers was when I went to the joint faculty of ESO and high school teachers, but the problems of certain basic vocational training students were discussed above all.

## My general impressions of these 3 weeks

::::: {style="display: flex; gap: 2em; align-items: stretch; justify-content: space-between;"}
::: {style="flex: 70%;"}
One thing I really liked was that Carlos asked me how I was doing at the end of the second day, and then asked me again at the end of the first week. I liked the feeling that he cared about how I felt in my first days. Furthermore, I have to say that there has been a very good chemistry between my mentor and me, with very similar life concerns and this helps a lot. In relation to the students, I have to say that the complexity is almost non-existent or I would say zero. Racial diversity is very limited or anecdotal with a Romanian and a girl from Moldova in 2nd year of high school and a Chinese girl in 4th year of ESO. In all 3 cases, the integration both at the language level and in the relationship with the other students is total, and all 3 are good students. Therefore, this almost zero complexity, without integration problems and absence of students with any cognitive or behavioral problems has led to quiet classes with nothing to highlight. In general, the students are paying attention, taking notes, and with nothing to report except for 4 or 5 times that Carlos has had to draw attention, always anonymously and without the need to repeat the call for attention. Only once has Carlos repeated the warning call with the threat of kicking her out of class. All these calls for attention have focused on high school, more so on 2 high school, while the group of 4 ESO could be defined as exemplary.

I also want to highlight that my relationship and interaction with the other high school teachers has been very good and there were always times to talk in the teachers' room about various matters, both school and extracurricular, or light conversation during the half hour of having coffee in the bar across the street, where we all went together. As I mentioned previously, the only *but* was the circumstance that Carlos (and I with him) only moved around the high school teachers' room and that limited my interaction with the rest of the ESO teachers beyond the two meetings that we all had together.

Finally, I would like to highlight my attendance at the high school and ESO faculty meeting that took place during my first week of internship. In this meeting, several high school and ESO topics were discussed but in a routine manner, but the main debate revolved around the problems of certain basic vocational training students who had difficulty following the school rules and their defiant attitude in some cases. The disparity in ways of addressing these problems was very evident and there was some tension in the faculty. Also my presence at the high school evaluation meeting after the first quarter exams has been quite formative since the way of analyzing certain situations of several students with low grades by several teachers has been varied depending on the teacher.
:::

## Agreed learning situations for the intervention phase

Finally, Carlos and I have already agreed on what didactic actions I will carry out during the intervention phase that will last 7 weeks from mid-February to mid-April 2026. These will be the following:

| 4th ESO | 2nd Baccalaureate |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| For [4 of ESO]{style="font-weight: bold;"}, I will do the point [The Earth in the Universe](#) included in the subject Biology and Geology. Description of the origin of the universe and its relationship with the stars that make up the solar system. Analysis and comparison of hypotheses about the origin of life, arguments. Discussion of the main research in the field of astrobiology. | For [2nd year of high school]{style="font-weight: bold;"}, the learning situation is the [quarterly optional subject on sustainable development goals](#). The SDG that will be discussed will be sustainable development goal number 13 “Climate Action” which is included in the thematic block of sustainable environment. In this specific action, Carlos has asked me to use a film or documentary in this teaching and in pairs to make a short presentation of the quotes from SDG 13, focusing attention on the implications of climate change and sustainability. |

Apart from these learning situations, I will do a class in English at the request of the English teacher (Montse) on climate change and the geopolitical and economic implications of the reduction of the North Pole ice cap. On the other hand, they have asked me to do a one-day intervention in a training cycle of landscape interpretation with an excursion to the Garraf mountain range to explain the reason for the physiography of the landscape from the point of view of geology.

I have also arranged to join Carlos in various activities. The first will be the visit that I will make with the 1st year high school students to the Faculty of Biology of the University of Barcelona on January 16, 2026, which will serve as a prelude to a biology learning situation that will take place during my second internship. Later, on January 26, he invited me to attend the exhibition of research work at the school. Finally, I will also go with Carlos on February 17 to the orientation sessions at the Viladecans Forum, which is like an exhibition of the research work carried out by the Viladecans city council, where each school in the city brings the 2 best research works of the high school students.
